key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early time-series data, enabling faster stability assessment of unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to shorten accelerated aging campaigns for perovskite solar materials while preserving cross-material generalization and interpretability.
method: Collected 167 metal-halide perovskite aging experiments under heat and illumination.
Converted 86k+ photoluminescence spectra into physics-informed features.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL stability for unseen samples.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset spanning different crystallinities and compositions and reportedly outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the physics-informed features and the training distribution, so extrapolation to new degradation regimes should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
